# Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho (Tika Abh07t)
**ID:** Tika Abh07t
**Section:** Tīkā Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho (tika-abh07)
**Collection:** Tika-Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho
**Title (English, from literature):** Compendium of Philosophy
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho* (also known as the *Abhidhammatthasaṅgaha*) was authored by Ācariya Anuruddha Thera as an authoritative compendium of Theravāda Abhidhamma doctrine [Sarao & Long 2017; Nguyen Van Hoa 2009; Cabezon 2017; IABU 2012]. The treatise systematizes Buddhist psychology and metaphysics, analyzing consciousness and derivative mental states (*cetasika*), unwholesome factors such as moral shamelessness (*ahirika*) and fearlessness of wrongdoing (*anottappa*), the ten defilements (*kilesa*: *lobha*, *dosa*, *moha*, *māna*, *diṭṭhi*, *vicikicchā*, *thīna*, *uddhacca*, *ahirika*, and *anottappa*), as well as sex faculties and gender [Sarao & Long 2017; Cabezon 2017]. In its treatment of causality, the text delineates the method of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppādanaya*), characterized by the simple occurrence of a state dependent on an antecedent condition, from the relational method (*paṭṭhānanaya*), noting that the twenty-four conditional relations can be subsumed under four primary conditions (*ārammaṇa*, *upanissaya*, *kamma*, and *atthi*) [Pande 1974; IABU 2012].
The text generated an extensive exegetical tradition, inspiring commentaries and sub-commentaries such as the *Abhidhammatthavibhāvinī-ṭīkā* (also known in Burma as the *Ṭīkā-kyaw*), the *Navanīta-ṭīkā* of Dhammānanda Kosambi, the *Abhidhammakaumudinī*, the *Sarūpa*, and the *Aṅkura* [Potter; Ruiz-Falqués 2015; Cabezon 2017; Pande 1974; IABU 2012]. In modern scholarship, it was published and translated for the Pali Text Society as the *Compendium of Philosophy* [Chan Yiu Wing 2013; Dhammajoti 2007; Watcharapratheep 2010], retranslated and revised by Nārada Thera and Bhikkhu Bodhi as *A Comprehensive Manual of Abhidhamma* [Nguyen Van Hoa 2009], edited with a Hindi exposition (*Abhidharmaprakāśinī*) by Rewatadhamma [Samtani 1971; Nguyen Van Hoa 2009], translated into Chinese by Ye Jun (*Shè āpǐdámó yì lùn*) [Tan Poh Beng 2015], and translated into Tibetan [Cabezon 2017].
No SuttaCentral record or curated parallels exist for the text. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records extensive Pali-internal text reuse (27,945 matching passages across 300 texts), sharing significant textual material with the *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā* (2,542 matches), Leḍī Sayāḍo's *Paramatthadīpanī* (1,939 matches), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (1,245 matches), the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā* (983 matches), the *Abhidhammāvatāro* (840 matches), and the *Visuddhimagga* (882 matches) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches meet the threshold score [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā (Tika Abh08t) (§1371_9–1375_2 ↔ §1694_22–1699_2); Leḍī sayāḍo gantha-saṅgaho Paramatthadīpanī (Anya E0301n) (§1130_3–1130_9 ↔ §549_0–549_5); Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi (Tika Abh09t) (§666–670 ↔ §39–47); Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Anya E0104n) (§1348_3–1349_5 ↔ §1234_3–1234_10); Abhidhammāvatāro (Tika Abh06t) (§954_0–954_10 ↔ §89_1–89_12); Visuddhimaggo (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Anya E0102n) (§919_0–919_8 ↔ §376_0–376_7); Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0517a) (§970_1–970_6 ↔ §745_2–745_8); Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh01a) (§1172_2–1172_8 ↔ §2417_3–2417_9)
**Sources**

- [Samtani 1971] N. H. Samtani, Arthaviniścaya-Sūtra & its Commentary (Nibandhana) (1971) — Mentions Hindi edition and translation Abhidharmaprakāśinī by Rewatadhamma.
- [Sarao & Long 2017] K. T. S. Sarao, Jeffery D. Long, eds., Buddhism and Jainism (2017) — Attests Anuruddha's authorship and details of the ten kilesas, hiri, and ottappa.
- [Nguyen Van Hoa 2009] Nguyen Van Hoa, Critical Study of Theory of Consciousness in Buddhism (2009) — Notes editions with the Vibhāvanīṭīkā and translations by Nārada and Bhikkhu Bodhi.
- [Watcharapratheep 2010] Phramaha Supat Watcharapratheep, Critical study of the concept of death in Buddhism (2010) — Cites English translations and manuals of the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho.
- [Potter] Karl H. Potter, Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies, Vol. 1 — Documents sub-commentaries including Navanītaṭīkā, Sarūpa, and Aṅkura.
- [Chan Yiu Wing 2013] Chan Yiu Wing, English Translation of the Dharmatrāta-Dhyāna-Sūtra (Yogācārabhūmi) (2013) — Cites the PTS translation Compendium of Philosophy.
- [Ruiz-Falqués 2015] Aleix Ruiz-Falqués, Firefly in the Bamboo Reed (2015) — Cites the Abhidhammatthavibhāvinī (Ṭīkā-kyaw) and Colombo edition of the text.
- [Dhammajoti 2007] K. L. Dhammajoti, Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma (2007) — Cites the Pali Text Society publication Compendium of Philosophy.
- [Cabezon 2017] Jose Ignacio Cabezon, Sexuality in Classical South Asian Buddhism (2017) — Discusses mental factors, sex faculties, gender, the Abhidhammakaumudinī commentary, and Tibetan translation.
- [Pande 1974] Govind Chandra Pande, Studies in the Origins of Buddhism (1974) — Quotes the text on paṭiccasamuppādanaya vs. paṭṭhānanaya, and notes Kosambi's Navanīta Tīkā.
- [Tan Poh Beng 2015] Tan Poh Beng, Survey of the Essence of Dhammasaṅgaṇī in Abhidhamma (2015) — Mentions Ye Jun's Chinese translation of the Abhidhammatthasaṅgaho.
- [IABU 2012] IABU, Unifying Buddhist Philosophical Views (2012) — Explicates Anuruddha's treatment of causal relations, conditions, and the reduction of conditions to four.
